Definition of Done (Proof Bar)
nodes.rationale: The repo's goal is proof, not theory: a run only counts as successful when art, engine, and proof artifacts (demo, validator, capstone walkthrough) are all verifiably green. This exists to stop the collection from being 'a pile of tips'.

nodes.label: STYLE.md Art Direction Sheet
nodes.rationale: A locked one-page style sheet (projection, light, palette, scale, anchor) is why 200 generated assets read as one game instead of a random asset dump; every asset prompt must reference it.

nodes.label: Obsidian & Gold UI Brand Layer
nodes.rationale: The in-game art uses a warm painterly palette, but the product UI (launcher, store, HUD chrome) uses a separate darker brand layer so the shell feels premium while the game world stays bright — a deliberate split between world-art style and product-UI style.

nodes.label: Skill Anatomy Template
nodes.rationale: A fixed anatomy (Overview / When to Use / Process / Rationalizations / Red Flags / Verification) is designed to stop an agent from cutting corners — naming the agent's typical excuse next to the reality prevents it from talking itself out of doing the work.

nodes.label: animated-sprite-generation Skill
nodes.rationale: Isometric animation is frame-based, not skeletal; ground tiles must never be animated because animating every ground tile tanks performance — only overlay objects (water/fire/flags) should loop.

nodes.label: asset-pipeline-automation Skill
nodes.rationale: Manual asset handling does not scale past a few sprites; a one-command clean->pack->validate pipeline run in CI stops atlas/JSON drift and missing-sprite holes from ever shipping.

nodes.label: autotiling-transitions Skill
nodes.rationale: Hard edges between terrains look like a checkerboard; a neighbor bitmask (N/E/S/W + corners) mapped to a transition-tile lookup gives a repeatable rule for hand-blended-looking seams instead of hand-placing every edge.

nodes.label: camera-pan-zoom-controls Skill
nodes.rationale: Users expect zoom to anchor at the cursor, not screen center, and without bounds clamping the player can pan into the void; snapping the final transform to whole pixels avoids tile shimmer.
